steps.title: See it
steps.text: The bishop moves diagonally, as far as it likes. It can't jump over pieces. Because it always moves diagonally, a bishop stays on squares of one colour for the whole game. The marked squares are every square it can reach.

steps.title: Try it
steps.text: Move the bishop to each marked square. Neither one can be reached in a single move.

pages.text: A bishop is strongest on a long, open diagonal. From a1 this bishop looks all the way across the board to h8.

A pin is an attack on a piece that can't move out of the way, because a more important piece stands behind it. Here the bishop goes to b5 and pins the knight to its king: if the knight moved, its king would be in check, and that is not allowed.
Your own pawns can block your bishop. This bishop on c1 can't move at all until a pawn gets out of its way. Move pawns early so your bishops can come out.

puzzles.hint: Follow the diagonal up and to the right from the bishop.

puzzles.prompt: Win the black queen in two moves.
puzzles.hint: Check the king along a diagonal, and look at what stands behind it.
Your king and knight guard every square around the black king. All that is missing is a check.
The black king has one free square. Take it away with one bishop, and then check with the other.
